meta.title: Touch Chord Expert Guitar chord-shape table

instrument.name: guitar
instrument.notes: Ukulele (G4 C4 E4 A4, reentrant) uses the same model but is out of scope.

selectionRules.otherwise: Choose a movable E-shape, A-shape or D-shape whose root string (6 / 5 / 4) can play the chord root (or whose lowest note is the slash bass). Prefer the candidate with the lowest barre fret; when a previous chord is known, prefer the shape whose fret is closest to that chord's fret (ties go to the lower fret, then E-shape, A-shape, D-shape).
selectionRules.slashRule: If a slash chord is not in the curated list, use a voicing of the upper chord whose lowest sounding note is the named bass. Prefer a familiar open inversion when one exists (3rd in the bass: C/E, G/B, D/F#, A/C#, E/G#, F/A, Am/C, Dm/F, Em/G; 5th in the bass: C/G, G/D, D/A, F/C, A/E). For other keys, start from the E-shape of the upper chord at fret R (the fret where the low E string plays the root): major /3 is x (R-1) (R+2) (R+1) R R; minor /3 is (R+3) x (R+2) R R R; major /2 (IV/V) is (R+2) x (R+2) (R+1) R R (F/G = 3x3211 or 333211); minor /2 is (R+2) x (R+2) R R R; /5 is x (R+2) plus the rest of the E-shape (F/C = x33211). Otherwise place the named bass under an existing open or movable shape, muting skipped strings. Keep span <= 4 and fingers <= 4 (a barre counts as one). If the bass cannot sit under a full voicing, keep the bass, the 3rd or sus tone, and the 7th/extension, and mark the grip simplified.
selectionRules.simplifiedRule: A grip is marked simplified when the full set of chord tones (except an omitted perfect 5th) cannot be played under the span/finger/fret limits. The 3rd (or sus tone) and the 7th, when the symbol has one, are never dropped. Altered 5ths (b5, #5) and the dim 5th stay in the grip.
selectionRules.leftHanded: A left-handed flip (strings reversed) is a later Settings option and is not in this table.
selectionRules.ukulele: Ukulele (G4 C4 E4 A4, reentrant high G) uses the same instrument-profile + shape model; it is out of scope here.
checks: Sounding pitch classes are a subset of the chord's tones (plus the slash bass) and include the root, the 3rd or sus tone, and the 7th/extension when the symbol has one.
The lowest sounding note is the root, or the named slash bass.
Fret span is 4 or less, excluding open strings.
At most 4 fingers, counting a barre as one.
